title: Eliminate straggler-induced queue freeze in unified scheduler
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Several customers (hosted + dedicated) reported intermittent 95th/99th token latency spikes and sustained request backlog growth. Root cause traced to a rare scheduler interaction where long-context or straggler requests cause a local queue to freeze while waiting on KV handoff + preemption logic, amplifying backlog and blocking short-latency flows. This ticket tracks the investigation, fix, tests, and rollout for a robust mitigation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: No reproduced queue-freeze in 48h deterministic stress test that previously failed 8/10 runs
95th token latency reduction >= 25% for mixed short+long workload in our canary region
No regressions in throughput on steady-state large-batch benchmarks (within 5%)
Automated integration test added to CI that simulates KV handoff + preemption ordering
Canary rollout plan with automated rollback on error rate or tail latency spikes
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy scheduler build with verbose tracing enabled to canary cluster
Start steady-state stream of short requests (seq len 64) at nominal production QPS
Inject a small number (3-7%) of long-context requests (seq len 8k) with aligned arrival patterns to trigger KV handoffs
Observe local dispatch queue growing and stall where preemption handoff waits on stale token that never clears
Collect scheduler traces, KV cache metrics, and per-tenant dispatch histograms
root_cause: A race between preemptive dequeue logic and the KV-cache handoff path. When a long-context request triggers a KV eviction and the handler takes a slow path (quantization fallback / disk spill in Private), preemption marks the batch as preempted but leaves an in-flight handoff token. The dequeue logic sees a non-empty queue and defers scheduling while waiting for token, but the token never resolves due to a missed wakeup in the handoff completion callback (edge case in backpressure code). This results in a local queue 'freeze' and backlog amplification under mixed-length workloads.
proposed_fix: Two-part fix: 1) Make handoff completion idempotent and ensure wakeups are performed on the scheduler's runloop thread (eliminate missed wakeup). 2) Add bounded stall detection in the dequeue path: if a handoff token blocks longer than threshold T (configurable, default 250ms), force a preemptive re-evaluation that either retries or moves pending short requests to a spill pool. The change is guarded by a feature flag and configurable thresholds to allow conservative rollout.
implementation_notes: Refactor handoff callbacks to post completion events to scheduler runloop via schedule_event() to avoid cross-thread missed signals
Introduce 'handoff_watchdog' per-queue that sets a metric and emits debug trace when blocked > 250ms
Add 'spill_pool' mechanism to temporarily reassign short requests from a frozen queue to a healthy executor without violating tenant isolation (soft preemption)
Keep the existing preemption semantics but ensure atomic transition state machine to prevent dual-wakeup or lost-complete scenarios
Change footprint minimal: new code path behind feature flag 'fix/straggler-queue-freeze' and rollout on canary first
rollout_plan: Merge PR to main with unit and integration tests (GH PR #9281)
Deploy to internal staging and run determinism + stress harness (24h)
Enable feature flag in canary region for 5% of tenant traffic, monitor for 48h
If metrics pass (tail latency, error rate, throughput), expand to 25% then 100% across Hosted
Coordinate with Dedicated & Private release channels: publish patch notes and optional hotfix package for on-prem customers
Full rollout targeted for runtime-1.22 stable release or sooner for critical customers
testing_plan: Unit tests for handoff completion idempotency and watcher state transitions
Deterministic replay harness that previously failed (replay ts: 2025-01-29 03:12 UTC) must pass >= 10/10 runs
Chaos test: simulate KV spill to disk and slow I/O on Private to ensure watchdog triggers and spill_pool takes effect
Performance test: mixed-workload benchmark comparing pre-fix vs post-fix for throughput and token latency
Add nightly fuzz runs for mixed short/long request distributions to CI
monitoring_and_alerting: New alert: scheduler_handoff_stall_rate > 0.5% over 5m in canary => auto-rollback
Dashboard: canary/hosted/dedicated tail-latency comparison and per-tenant backlog heatmap
Log-level: handoff_watchdog emits structured trace id + queue id for quick triage
Oncall runbook: steps to toggle feature flag, trigger manual spill, and collect traces for ENG-sre
